questions.prompt: What benefit of the three-dimensional framework does the author identify?
questions.promptZh: 作者指出三维框架有什么益处？
options: It can also evaluate jobs that may be psychologically rich despite low happiness or meaning.
It proves all jobs have identical happiness and meaning.
It replaces every job evaluation with salary.
It guarantees every worker will love their job.
optionsZh: 也可评价快乐或意义不高但可能心理丰富的工作。
证明所有工作的快乐与意义都相同。
用薪水取代所有工作评价。
analyses: A professional sphere与could still be good给出应用和可能性。
B 不同维度正可产生差异。
C 框架不只考虑薪水。
D some和could不支持全员保证。

vocabulary.meaning: 职业领域；与工作有关的范围
vocabulary.context: 三维框架可用于此领域，不代表每项工作都满足每个维度。
vocabulary.example: The framework can be applied to the professional sphere.

questions.evidenceQuote: My guess is that many art directors, editors, and writers would say that their jobs are interesting, creative, and psychologically rich. This may be a reason why people continue in such professions. The benefit of the three-dimension framework for defining a good life is that it can be applied to the professional sphere, explaining why some jobs low in happiness or meaning could still be good— psychologically rich—jobs.

questions.prompt: Which two vacation options are contrasted?
questions.promptZh: 文中对照哪两种假期选择？
options: Two identical all-inclusive tours.
A luxury cruise and a daily commute.
Two compulsory work assignments.
An all-inclusive luxury tour and a low-key backpacking trip.
optionsZh: 两次完全相同的全包旅行。
全包豪华旅行与朴素背包游。
analyses: A 问句明确提出两种不同方式。
B 通勤不在选项中。
C 文中是度假选择。
D 两项对应all-inclusive luxury tour和low-key backpacking trip。

vocabulary.meaning: 全包的；主要安排包含在旅行服务中
vocabulary.context: 此处修饰旅行形式，不保证世界上每个费用都无条件包含。
vocabulary.example: They compared an all-inclusive tour with backpacking.

questions.evidenceQuote: For your next vacation, would you like to take an all-inclusive luxury tour or a low-key backpacking trip? The all-inclusive tour is easy. All you have to do is pay and show up. The tour company has a plan.

questions.prompt: Why is the all-inclusive tour described as easy in this account?
questions.promptZh: 本段为何说全包旅行轻松？
options: The traveller must independently arrange every activity.
The company has a plan and the traveller mainly pays and shows up.
It guarantees every possible journey is free of problems.
The traveller must carry all food without assistance.
optionsZh: 旅客必须独立安排每项活动。
公司已有计划，旅客主要付钱并到场。
保证所有旅程没有任何问题。
旅客必须无人帮助自行携带全部食物。
analyses: A 这更接近后文对背包游的描述。
B pay and show up及company has a plan解释easy。
C easy不是绝对无问题保证。
D 本段没有此要求。

vocabulary.context: 与pay并列，形容示例中旅客需做的基本事情。
vocabulary.example: Participants pay and show up while the company provides the plan.
collocations: The tour company has a plan

questions.evidenceQuote: For your next vacation, would you like to take an all-inclusive luxury tour or a low-key backpacking trip? The all-inclusive tour is easy. All you have to do is pay and show up. The tour company has a plan.

questions.prompt: What makes backpacking harder in the contrast?
questions.promptZh: 对照中，什么使背包游更难？
options: It provides identical arrangements before departure.
It requires no decisions from the traveller.
Accommodation is uncertain and the traveller plans much of the trip.
The company arranges every step from morning to night.
optionsZh: 出发前提供完全相同的安排。
住宿不确定，旅客要自己规划大部分行程。
公司从早到晚安排每一步。
analyses: A 不知道最终住处与固定安排不同。
B plan...by yourself表示需自己决策。
C 两项紧接harder说明自助安排和不确定性。
D 公司安排娱乐属于前面的全包旅游。

vocabulary.context: 这里是不确定会住到何种地方，不是对某个人的特殊照顾。
vocabulary.example: Backpackers may not know what accommodations they will find.

questions.evidenceQuote: They’ll entertain you from morning to night—you can just sit back and enjoy. The backpacking trip would be a lot harder. You don’t know what kind of accommodations you’ll end up with. You have to plan pretty much everything by yourself.

questions.prompt: What did Inbar and Tullett use the trip metaphors to describe?
questions.promptZh: Inbar与Tullett用旅行比喻描述什么？
options: Only the cost of flights between countries.
The popularity of music across generations.
The self-esteem equation and survey percentages.
A happy life and a psychologically rich life.
optionsZh: 快乐人生和心理丰富人生。
analyses: A 旅行是比喻，并非仅分析票价。
B 音乐属于前章其他段落。
C 此句不是公式讨论。
D used those trip metaphors...happy life and psychologically rich life明确对应。

vocabulary.meaning: 比喻；借一类事物帮助理解另一类事物
vocabulary.context: 游轮与背包游用于描述人生类型，不表示人生真的必须乘游轮。
vocabulary.example: They used trip metaphors to describe different kinds of life.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the podcast Two Psychologists Four Beers, Yoel Inbar and Alexa Tullett used those trip metaphors to describe a happy life and a psychologically rich life. A happy life is like a Caribbean cruise. Everything is planned. You get fed, and everything is taken care of.

questions.prompt: How broad is the reported finding about the ideal-life descriptions?
questions.promptZh: 关于理想人生描述，报告的范围有多大？
options: All respondents in all nine countries gave identical answers.
Many American participants wrote descriptions resembling a luxury cruise.
Only nine Americans participated in the entire study.
The survey showed every American has taken a luxury cruise.
optionsZh: 九国全部受访者答案一致。
许多美国参与者的描述像豪华游轮生活。
整个研究只有九名美国人。
调查证明所有美国人都坐过豪华游轮。
analyses: A many Americans不能扩大成九国全部。
B 原句同时说明九国参与者及许多美国人的描述。
C nine修饰countries，不是美国人数。
D resembled描述理想生活相似性，并非实际乘船经历。

vocabulary.context: 此处是理想生活描述与豪华游轮的比喻相似，不是本人实际旅行记录。
vocabulary.example: Some descriptions resembled a comfortable cruise.

questions.evidenceQuote: When we asked participants from nine countries to describe an ideal life, many Americans wrote about a life that resembled a luxury cruise. For instance, an eighteen-year-old University of Virginia student wrote, “On a beach with lots of money and a happy family. I would not want to worry about working as I would have been successful enough so I would not have to work anymore.” For many, a vacation (and an ideal life) is for relaxation and rejuvenation, for being served and entertained.

questions.prompt: What does the author say a vacation is for many people?
questions.promptZh: 作者说假期对许多人意味着什么？
options: Relaxation and rejuvenation, with service and entertainment.
Guaranteed hardship and uncertainty for everyone.
A compulsory effort to avoid all enjoyment.
The same experience as a full-time job.
optionsZh: 放松、恢复活力，并接受服务和娱乐。
对所有人保证艰难和不确定。
analyses: A for many及relaxation and rejuvenation限定人群与用途。
B for many不是everyone，内容也反转。
C being entertained不等于避免享受。
D 未说假期与工作完全相同。

vocabulary.meaning: 恢复活力；使身心重新有精神
vocabulary.context: 这里与放松并列，不是年龄生物学意义上的倒退。
vocabulary.example: A relaxing break can offer a sense of rejuvenation.

questions.evidenceQuote: When we asked participants from nine countries to describe an ideal life, many Americans wrote about a life that resembled a luxury cruise. For instance, an eighteen-year-old University of Virginia student wrote, “On a beach with lots of money and a happy family. I would not want to worry about working as I would have been successful enough so I would not have to work anymore.” For many, a vacation (and an ideal life) is for relaxation and rejuvenation, for being served and entertained.

questions.prompt: What is the backpacking trip compared with?
questions.promptZh: 背包游被比作什么？
options: A mathematically guaranteed happy life.
Only a perfectly planned cruise.
A psychologically rich trip.
A survey of occupational salaries.
optionsZh: 数学上保证快乐的人生。
analyses: A 没有数学保证。
B 对照的是另一旅行类型。
C is like明确将心理丰富旅程比作背包游。
D 不是薪酬调查。

vocabulary.meaning: 心理丰富的；具有多样和引人思考的经历
vocabulary.context: 此处通过背包游的选择与不确定性比喻，不保证每次旅行都愉快。
vocabulary.example: A challenging trip may be psychologically rich.

questions.evidenceQuote: A psychologically rich trip is like a backpacking trip. You have to plan it all by yourself. You can choose what you want to do. At the same time, you never know what to expect, and you might encounter something bad.

questions.prompt: How does the narrator assess the seventy-hour bus ride?
questions.promptZh: 叙述者怎样评价70小时的巴士行程？
options: He calls it the easiest part of the holiday.
He says it was not exactly fun.
He says it lasted exactly seventy days.
He reports every passenger enjoyed it equally.
optionsZh: 称它是假期最轻松部分。
报告所有乘客同样享受。
analyses: A not exactly fun与最轻松相反。
B 这是作者对漫长行程的个人评价。
C seventy-hour是小时而非天。
D 没有全体乘客评价。

vocabulary.meaning: 并不怎么有趣；委婉表达负面体验
vocabulary.context: 作者用语气缓和的说法评价长途车程。
vocabulary.example: The long overnight journey was not exactly fun.

questions.evidenceQuote: We did a thirty-day Greyhound bus trip from LA to San Francisco to Seattle to Mount Rushmore, South Dakota to Chicago to Niagara Falls to New York City to Washington D.C. By the time we were in D.C., we realized we were almost out of time, so the final three days were an almost nonstop bus ride from D.C. to LA. A seventy-hour bus ride…not exactly fun.

questions.prompt: Why did the travellers stay in youth hostels?
questions.promptZh: 旅行者为何住青年旅舍？
options: Their budget limited what they could afford.
A tour company had reserved luxury rooms for them.
They owned all the hostels along the route.
They were required by a research protocol to stay there.
optionsZh: 预算限制使他们只能负担青年旅舍。
旅行公司为他们预订了豪华房。
他们拥有沿途所有旅舍。
analyses: A all we could afford明确给费用限制。
B 前句没有提前订酒店。
C 未说拥有旅舍。
D 这是旅行回忆而非实验规定。

vocabulary.meaning: 负担得起；有足够的钱支付
vocabulary.context: 此处说明有限预算下可选住宿范围。
vocabulary.example: Their budget meant they could afford only youth hostels.

questions.evidenceQuote: We didn’t have any reservations for hotels in advance, so we looked for somewhere to stay once we arrived in Los Angeles, then in San Francisco, then in Seattle. All we could afford were youth hostels. The Greyhound stations were almost always in downtown areas, which were not the safest back in 1988. With our limited budget and minimal English, we encountered many scary moments.

He describes downtown areas as not the safest back in 1988.

他说1988年那些市中心区域不算最安全。
analyses: A back in 1988限定历史语境，不能自动作现时判断。
B 没有当前完整排名。
C not the safest并非每站都受害。
D 地点与1988年的限定均保留。

vocabulary.meaning: 市中心；城市商业中心区域
vocabulary.context: 作者描述1988年的经历，不构成当前安全建议。
vocabulary.example: The stations were often in downtown areas in the account.

questions.evidenceQuote: We didn’t have any reservations for hotels in advance, so we looked for somewhere to stay once we arrived in Los Angeles, then in San Francisco, then in Seattle. All we could afford were youth hostels. The Greyhound stations were almost always in downtown areas, which were not the safest back in 1988. With our limited budget and minimal English, we encountered many scary moments.

questions.prompt: What did the man near the youth hostel ask the narrator?
questions.promptZh: 青年旅舍附近的男子向叙述者提出什么请求？

To take a photograph at a festival.
To purchase a bus pass for thirty days.
To accompany the police to the White House.

B 拍照是之后芝加哥另一段经历。
C 巴士通票是旅程背景。

questions.evidenceQuote: In New York City, a guy just outside our youth hostel on Forty-Second Street approached me and asked if he could borrow $20. A Citibank was right there. He said he would just go to the bank, get cash, and pay me back. “Follow me,” he said.

questions.prompt: Where was the bank in relation to the encounter?
questions.promptZh: 银行相对于这次遭遇位于哪里？

It was inside the narrator's hostel room.
It was nearby.
It was in another city.

就在叙述者旅舍房间里。

B 不等于位于房间内。

D 未提另一城市。

vocabulary.meaning: 就在那儿；离说话地点很近

questions.prompt: Who says 'Follow me' in the episode?

The narrator's host in Wisconsin.

The stranger who asked to borrow money.

questions.evidenceQuote: In New York City, a guy just outside our youth hostel on Forty-Second Street approached me and asked if he could borrow $20. A Citibank was right there. He said he would just go to the bank, get cash, and pay me back. “Follow me,” he said.

questions.prompt: What did the narrator do after the man's invitation to follow him?
questions.promptZh: 男子请他跟随后，叙述者做了什么？

questions.prompt: Where did the travellers fall asleep after arriving in Washington?

options: Inside the White House during a tour.
On the bus before leaving New York.
